title: What Happens in the First 3.6 Seconds After Gunfire Is Detected?
summary: As the number of active shooter incidents reaches an all time high, prioritizing employee and visitor safety becomes increasingly more important, everyday. However, does this protection still have to come with an exorbitant price tag, as gunshot detection technology has evolved?
body_markdown:
3.6 seconds. That's how quickly AmberBox can detect a confirmed gunshot and initiate its automated emergency response sequence. In an active shooter incident, those first seconds are critical. The challenge isn't simply recognizing that something happened. It's making sure the right people know immediately and that emergency response begins without delay.


#### The Minutes Before the First Call


Many emergency response plans focus on how quickly police arrive. But the response timeline begins much earlier. On average, approximately five minutes can pass between a gunshot and the first call to police. During those minutes, people may be trying to understand what they heard, locate the source, find safety, or contact emergency services. Every step requires time. In a rapidly developing emergency, time is the resource organizations cannot recover.


#### From Gunshot to Emergency Response


AmberBox automates the actions that traditionally depend on someone recognizing an incident and initiating a call. When a detector confirms gunfire, the system begins a coordinated response sequence in 3.6 seconds: • Identifies the precise location of the gunshot • Sends call, text, and email alerts to designated security personnel • Automatically initiates an E911 call Opens a conference bridge connecting key personnel with police dispatch The result is immediate awareness and a direct connection to emergency responders.


#### Location Changes Everything


Knowing that gunfire occurred is important. Knowing exactly where it occurred gives responders information they can act on. In large facilities, the difference between a general building alert and precise location intelligence can be significant. A manufacturing plant may span hundreds of thousands of square feet. A corporate campus may include multiple buildings. A shopping center may have dozens of entrances and corridors. AmberBox provides location information alongside the notification, helping security teams and emergency responders coordinate their next steps. Automated response is not about replacing trained security professionals. It is about giving them actionable information sooner. Security teams can focus on coordinating the response instead of spending the first moments trying to establish what happened. Police dispatch receives the emergency notification without waiting for someone inside the building to make the initial call. And the conference bridge creates a direct communication channel between key personnel and dispatch. No security technology can eliminate every threat or guarantee an outcome. But organizations can influence how quickly they recognize an incident and begin responding. AmberBox was built to shorten that critical window. 3.6 seconds from detection to action.
